lines: Thai Duong and Bruce Dang of hacking firm Calif argue AI is collapsing the window between finding a software flaw and exploiting it, so defenses built around patching and detection are no longer enough.

They say models good at coding and debugging are inherently good at hacking, so the offensive risk can't be separated from the productivity gains; the PHP2Shell bug, dormant in a language used by about 70% of websites, is their example.

In their view, AI agents can reverse-engineer public patches on GitHub into working exploits before users update, and attacks have shifted from surgical intrusions to mass compromises spreading at machine speed.

They claim AI analysis of long-hardened codebases turns up as many as ten times more vulnerabilities than previously estimated, while formal verification still can't scale to software as large and fast-changing as browsers.

Today's edge belongs to 'centaur' hackers pairing human intuition with AI, which they expect to be short-lived, and the attacker-defender asymmetry persists because defenders must cover every entry point while keeping systems running.
title: PHP2Shell Won't Be the Last Big AI Cybersecurity Risk
